key_insight: SG-DOR builds scene graphs from instance-segmented organ point clouds that explicitly encode physical attachments and view-dependent occlusion relations, enabling robots to rank which organs block a target fruit from a given direction.
problem_solved: Identifies which plant organs occlude a target fruit depending on viewpoint in dense crop canopies—solving the need for direction-conditioned, relational occlusion reasoning for safe and efficient robotic harvesting.
method: Input: per-organ instance-segmented 3D point clouds of plant organs.
Graph-based model that predicts two relation types: physical attachments and direction-conditioned occlusion (formulated as an occlusion-ranking task).
Scene-graph decoder that outputs ranked occluders conditioned on a query direction for downstream planning and intervention.
impact: Provides an interpretable, relational representation that enables occlusion-aware perception and planning for agricultural robots and other manipulation tasks in cluttered 3D environments, improving end-effector routing and success rates.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: point-cloud input → graph construction → relation prediction → ranked occluders.
Before/after illustration of a pepper plant: occluders color-coded by rank from a given viewpoint.
Model architecture block diagram highlighting direction-conditioned module and scene-graph decoder.
Bar chart comparing occlusion-ranking accuracy and manipulation success vs. baseline methods.
paper_title: SG-DOR: Learning Scene Graphs with Direction-Conditioned Occlusion Reasoning for Pepper Plants
paper_authors: Rohit Menon, Niklas Mueller-Goldingen, Sicong Pan, Gokul Krishna Chenchani, Maren Bennewitz
